## Concrete breaking changes and best-practice findings

### A. Removed click option affects deterministic replay

Puppeteer 25 removes `MouseOptions.clickCount`. Actual calls exist at:

- `packages/core/src/executor/step-handlers/fill.ts:87`: triple-click selection before typing a resolved secret.
- `packages/core/src/executor/step-handlers/fill-element.ts:342`: triple-click selection before filling.
- `packages/core/src/executor/step-handlers/click.ts:65`: conditional single-click option.

The migration must preserve replacement rather than append semantics for text entry, secret non-disclosure, actual mouse event behavior, and deterministic replay behavior. A typed rename alone is insufficient evidence. The supported `count` option sends a number of clicks; characterize triple-selection behavior rather than assuming identical event sequences to the removed option. [MouseClickOptions](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.mouseclickoptions).

Repository-wide targeted searches found no use of removed `Browser.isConnected()`, `Puppeteer.product`, cookie `sameParty`, or calls to newly asynchronous `PuppeteerNode.executablePath()` / `defaultArgs()`. `executablePath` launch-option fields and the recorder's CDP `versionInfo.product` are different APIs and should not be rewritten merely because the names match. ESM is already the project baseline. Header newline normalization and transitive CDP/BiDi updates still belong in upgrade regression review. [Breaking changes](https://pptr.dev/CHANGELOG).

### B. Obsolete Page.target is used for popup identity, not session construction

`browser/agent-controller.ts:874` uses `browser.waitForTarget(target => target.opener() === page.target())`; line 1196 compares the live page target inside a browser `targetcreated` listener. The controller stores captures by `Target`, converts via `target.page()`, and falls back to `target.url()`.

The documented replacement for spawned pages is `PageEvent.Popup`. This requires redesigning listener attachment and removal across adopted-page swaps, deduplicating by Page identity, registering before click dispatch, and preserving bounded about:blank URL settlement. Preserve existing behavior: same-site popups are held for explicit policy-checked adoption; third-party popups close; refs and settling state follow the active page. Existing controller tests cover several of these behaviors and must run against v25. [Page.target deprecation](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.page.target).

The screenshot path already uses `page.createCDPSession()` with `detach()` in `finally` at `agent-controller.ts:583`. Preserve its opt-in, raw-pixel grant, byte/dimension caps, overlay cleanup, and audit semantics. Do not replace working page-scoped CDP with an incorrectly scoped browser session. [Page.createCDPSession](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.page.createcdpsession).

### C. Recorder session lookup has an unsafe fallback

`workflow/recorder/popup-handler.ts:213-236` casts a CDPSession to a shape containing `_connection` or a `connection` object, then calls `.session(sessionId)`. If lookup fails it returns the browser-level CDPSession as though it were the popup session. Flat transport does not make browser and page session scopes interchangeable; subsequent page Runtime/Page commands can be directed to the wrong session.

The supported public API is `browserCDP.connection()?.session(sessionId)`: `connection` is a method, not the object assumed by the current cast. `_connection` compatibility probing and browser-session substitution should be removed. The design must address attachment timing, exact target/session correlation, failure reporting, listener removal, and detach ownership. Public SessionAttached events are another available mechanism to evaluate. [CDPSession.connection](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.cdpsession.connection), [Connection.session](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.connection.session).

`workflow/recorder/session.ts:225` uses `browser.target().createCDPSession()` for browser-wide target discovery. **Browser.target is documented and is not the obsolete Page.target API.** Retain a legitimate browser-scoped session for browser-wide commands; do not mechanically replace this call with a page session. Main-page session creation already uses `mainPage.createCDPSession()`, and main target identity is read through `Target.getTargetInfo`. [Browser.target](https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.browser.target).

### D. Locator frame identity depends on a private field

`locator/injected-host.ts:120-121` reads `(frame as Frame & { _id?: string })._id`. Any requested non-main frame uses that mapping. Follow-up inspection found no persisted locator frame-ID contract in protocol schemas and no production caller supplying a non-main frameId; the earlier concern about saved frame identity was hypothetical, not an implemented contract. Replace the private field with session-local opaque tokens keyed by public Frame object identity and retain the main sentinel. Do not introduce ambiguous URL/name matching or a needless persisted/CDP mapping subsystem.

### E. Two launch paths and incomplete startup cleanup

`browser/launcher.ts` and `workflow/recorder/session.ts` each call `puppeteer.launch` directly. Recorder bypasses launch-option validation, minimum-version validation, shared user-simulation arguments, shared startup timeout, provider logging, and shared session cleanup. Managed selection and compatibility must reach both. Sharing transport/process ownership can still allow recorder-specific headful/profile behavior.

`browser/launcher.ts:44-77` races launch against a timeout without cancelling the underlying launch or disposing a late successful browser; the timeout is also not cleared on success. `browser/provider.ts:65` resolves/creates a profile before discovery/version/launch failure, without a corresponding failure cleanup path. Recorder similarly creates recording state before launch and has no enclosing startup rollback. These are lifecycle refactor concerns, not proven runtime failures from this audit.

`browser/session.ts` bounds graceful close and uses Windows process-tree termination. Its POSIX force-kill condition reads `child.killed` after signalling; signalling is not proof of process exit. Cleanup should be tested against actual process completion. Handle collections and event listeners also require ownership review under navigation, popup adoption, crashes, and startup cancellation.

## Confirmed product decisions

The user confirmed the initial decisions and then approved the shared architecture, command/config/storage direction, five features, and older-external compatibility policy. Their later update correction supersedes earlier update-check proposals:

1. Use the `@puppeteer/browsers` programmatic API when available.
2. Offer an interactive download when Chrome is missing; automation must install explicitly.
3. Prefer Yantra-managed Chrome when both managed and external installations exist.
4. Check for updates **only through the explicit update command**, report the proposed build, and ask before replacing. The user's later diagnostic request adds `browser update --check` for metadata-only availability and `browser check` for fresh local compatibility. No automatic checks, notifications from other sessions, or multi-version support.
5. Use Chrome for Testing Stable as the managed browser.
6. When newer Stable differs from Puppeteer's tested build, run a capability check and proceed with a notice if it passes.

The complete plan resolves storage to the Yantra data/browser subtree, source selection to config.yaml, and commands to browser list/install/use/check/update (including update --check) with shared one-run overrides where consumed. Actual updates/install replacement refuse while any managed browser run is active; metadata-only update --check is allowed and never performs repair/cleanup. There is one logical installation; initial/candidate installations each occupy disjoint opaque child cache roots and only one ready record selects one. Internal candidate/previous state exists only for a replacement transaction and is never a browser-version list, pin, rollback or retention feature.

Final scope dispositions:

- Preserve existing external Chrome/Chromium discovery with local capability validation; managed availability follows upstream supported host platform/architecture and is Stable-only.
- No version retention, rollback or pinning surface. Refuse replacement while managed browser use is active; preserve previous ready installation on precommit failure.
- Reuse installed compatible browsers offline. Configured unsupported proxy handling fails explicitly before direct network; no new proxy package or OS installation is silently added.
- Store installation selection only in config.yaml, with persistent browser use and nonpersistent per-command browser overrides.
- Preserve current user-simulation launch behavior; no separate stealth or interaction-policy redesign.
- Named plan is `.spec-lite/plan_puppeteer_browser_management.md`.

The approved breakdown is allocated as FEAT-042 through FEAT-046 in the named plan. Feature agents will fill its spec links; no implementation statuses have been changed.

## Final feasibility constraints incorporated into the plan

The named plan incorporates these constraints and simplifies the earlier concurrency proposal to one installation with replacement exclusion.

The pinned browsers implementation exposes `install()` options for `cacheDir`, browser/platform/build identity, progress, providers and related installation settings, but **no AbortSignal, timeout, or separate temporary archive directory**. A cancellation design must not invent those options. A naked timeout race would leave a live download/extraction modifying disk after Yantra reports cancellation. [Pinned install implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/puppeteer-v25.10.0/packages/browsers/src/install.ts).

Final integration: a Yantra-owned Node helper calls the programmatic `@puppeteer/browsers` API and reports bounded structured progress/result messages over IPC. This satisfies the confirmed API preference; it does not execute the browsers CLI, `npx`, or a global installation. Spawn with an explicit argument array, no shell, and hidden Windows process behavior. Core's existing TypeScript build preserves source directories under `dist`, so a dedicated helper module can be resolved relative to `import.meta.url` and shipped under the existing package `files: [dist]` contract. No extra runtime bundler or worker package is needed for this arrangement.

Cancellation must terminate and await the owned helper **and any extraction descendants** before deleting partial content or releasing operation ownership. Unix process-group and Windows process-tree termination need platform tests; child exit alone does not prove an extraction descendant stopped. Parent disconnect/crash and stale-operation recovery require explicit owner identity and liveness handling. Metadata resolution using an upstream API without cancellation needs the same bounded owned-process boundary, or a separate truly abortable fetch boundary; it must not merely race a timer.

Final storage supersedes the earlier direct-managed-root and staging/promotion proposals: **every** initial install or update candidate receives a disjoint child package cache `dataDir()/browsers/installation-<opaque-id>`. `install()` receives that child as cacheDir, never `dataDir()/browsers` itself. Coordination/ready/transaction files live outside those child caches. After extraction, executable validation and local compatibility succeed, atomically publish the single ready record naming one child and its relative executable. Never select a candidate from directory presence or upstream `getInstalledBrowsers()` alone. Never rewrite the previous ready build in place. After publication remove exactly its previous sibling child, never the managed root or any common ancestor. There is no directory promotion and no version-history registry.

The upstream cache can record absolute executable paths in `.metadata`; blindly renaming trees or trusting stored absolute paths after data relocation would be incorrect. The final plan keeps each child cache at its final name and stores relative readiness identity. On data relocation recompute the default-provider executable path from current child root/browser/platform/build; repair owned stale metadata only if a subsequent API call requires it. Do not trust a stale `InstalledBrowser.executablePath` or `.metadata` mapping. A relocated Yantra cache directory may be on another volume; the earlier cross-root staging approach is superseded. [Pinned cache implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/puppeteer-v25.10.0/packages/browsers/src/Cache.ts).

On cancellation/failure, remove only the exact transaction-owned candidate child cache after the helper and extraction descendants have terminated; never clear the managed root. Reconcile leftovers under coordination before retry, because the package may treat existing layout as installed. Explicit custom paths inside Yantra's managed tree still obey readiness and active-use reservation checks rather than bypass ownership validation.

Use existing `proper-lockfile` for a short coordination mutex and process-owned active-run reservations; do not assume it natively provides reader/writer locking. Replacement claims exclusive mutation only when no managed run is active; otherwise reject with stop-and-retry guidance. While mutation is active, new managed launches fail as operation-in-progress. Concurrent requests cannot expose partial readiness. This is one-installation exclusion, not per-version leases/pruning. Stale reservation recovery verifies liveness rather than treating age as permission to delete a running browser.

Proxy behavior is explicit at the download boundary. The upstream optional `proxy-agent` import can fall back to direct networking when the package is absent; Yantra must not silently bypass a configured proxy. The final minimal plan adds no new proxy dependency and fails before browser network calls if configured proxy handling is unavailable, with a typed actionable error and locally installed-browser guidance. [Pinned HTTP implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/puppeteer-v25.10.0/packages/browsers/src/httpUtil.ts).

The five implementation features are approved and allocated in the named plan: Puppeteer API migration; unified launch/selection and compatibility; managed Stable installation; switching and doctor visibility; and explicit managed update. Source changes and dependency installation remain outside this planning session.
